UNVERIFIED, found in this session, deliberately NOT 'fixed'. A second, independent inaccuracy in the same release record, distinct from the effective_commit history above. verification.release.legacy_tags records v0.3.2 as 86655102a92cd4afb92f9e965b6078a249bb2192, which is the annotated tag OBJECT, not a commit; the commit it points at is 75cfffb583bc0a241aa3270aa207dcdc21833cf4. The other six entries (v0.1.0 through v0.3.1) are lightweight tags whose recorded value is already the commit, so v0.3.2 is inconsistent with them and the field's stated meaning is 'full commit'. Verified by comparing every entry against git rev-list -n1. A repair was probed in a full clone with real history and tags against the alpha.16 tool: setting the entry to the real commit changes the release finding from 'Release convention history boundary changed; preserve original applicability' to 'Previously recorded legacy tag mapping was erased or changed'. That is strictly worse, because legacy_tags is a retained observation and the release contract requires retained tag/commit observations to remain unchanged - current refs cannot prove historical immutability, and correcting a record to match today's refs would assert a history the record never published. The change was therefore discarded and the observation recorded instead. This is a correctable-in-principle defect that the retained-observation rule makes uncorrectable in place; it belongs with the maintainer and, if useful, upstream. Does not by itself change the release finding, which remains as described above.
